arxiv-2603-09945: Yundi Zhang and coauthors skip image reconstruction entirely and analyse heart scans straight from undersampled k-space data. Standard cardiac MRI first rebuilds a full image, an ill posed step that adds artifacts and loses information. Their k-MTR framework aligns undersampled signals and full images in one shared latent space. Trained on a large simulated cohort, it matches strong rivals at phenotype regression, disease sorting and anatomy outlining.
arxiv-2603-10045: Chong-Sen Huang and coauthors present a sharp, conservative 3D method for moving contact lines on complex solid shapes. Their scheme couples a geometric volume of fluid approach with embedded boundaries, handling cells that hold liquid, gas and solid together. A redistribution step removes the harsh time step limit from tiny cut cells while keeping mass exact. A paraboloid prefit improves curvature estimates, and contact angle hysteresis is included for realism.
arxiv-2603-10245: Epp, Molinari and Raisch study formation control of mixed self driven agents that share one wireless channel. Rather than dodging clashes with one by one sends, they use channel superposition so each receiver gets a weighted blend of neighbour signals at once. Agents update their target spots from those blends and track them between notes. A rate rule for how often agents talk ensures the group settles into the set formation, eased further when tracking swings help.
arxiv-2603-10345: Kseniia Golubenko and co-authors present SOCOL:14C-Ex, a three-dimensional dynamical model of how radiocarbon is produced in the air and carried around the globe. Such modelling matters for Miyake events, sharp tree-ring radiocarbon spikes from extreme solar particle events that serve as precise dating tie-points. The team computed response curves for a reference event, then fitted seven strong events from the past 14 millennia. Their fits give likely strengths and dates for each, confirming the 12351 BC event as the strongest overall.
arxiv-2603-11245: Xuhui Zhou and coauthors run the first human study of the simulation-to-reality gap in language-model user simulators, the stand-in users now used to test and grade AI agents. Running a standard interactive benchmark protocol with 451 real participants, they score 31 simulators on a new index of resemblance to real user behavior. Simulated users prove excessively cooperative, stylistically uniform, and short on frustration or ambiguity, easing tasks and inflating agent success. Their feedback runs uniformly more positive than the nuanced judgments real humans give across quality dimensions.
arxiv-2603-11545: Saini and Bishwas present an adaptive framework that answers multimodal queries by orchestrating tools under one supervisor. The supervisor splits each query and sends subtasks to tools fit for each modality, then merges results. Text-only queries use learned routing via RouteLLM; other paths lean on small-model decomposition. On 2,847 queries across 15 task types, time to a correct answer falls 72 percent. Rework drops 85 percent and cost 67 percent against a matched baseline, with accuracy held even.
arxiv-2603-11845: Azzouz and co-authors ask whether clean speech, recorded away from MRI noise, can drive articulatory inversion. MRI scanners corrupt their own audio, so inversion models usually train on denoised MRI speech. The team aligns clean and MRI recordings of the same speaker saying the same sentences. A model trained on denoised MRI speech is then tested on both kinds of audio. Clean speech works well, reaching an RMSE of 1.56 mm, close to the MRI-based score.
arxiv-2603-12145: Karten, Appapogu, and Jin automate the slow craft of writing high-performance RL environments. Their closed loop starts from a generic prompt template and checks each build in layers. Property, interaction, and rollout tests guide repair rounds until the copy matches the source. Five environments pass through three workflows, from direct translation to a brand-new card game build. Cross-backend policy transfer confirms no sim-to-sim gap in any case. Environment overhead falls below a small share of training time at large scale.
arxiv-2603-12245: Haji-Ali and co-authors give Diffusion Transformers an elastic latent interface for flexible compute budgets. Standard DiTs lock cost to image size and spread work evenly across spatial tokens. ELIT inserts a learnable latent sequence of variable length between the image tokens. Light cross-attention layers read and write between spatial tokens and latents, favoring key regions. Training drops tail latents at random, so early latents learn global structure and late ones add detail. At run time the latent count can flex to match the compute at hand.
arxiv-2603-12445: Okonoda, Martinez, Dalal, and Shamir unmask bias in CNN analysis of cancer pathology images. CNNs score well at telling cancer types apart, yet their inner logic stays opaque. The team tested 13 much-used cancer datasets with four common CNN designs across cancer kinds. Cropped background segments with no clinical content served as a null test set. Models still scored high accuracy on those empty crops, at times above nine in ten. Some designs proved more bias-prone than others, a warning for standard evaluation practice.
arxiv-2603-12545: Alam and co-authors ask why vision-language models stay brittle at basic spatial reasoning. Models ace general benchmarks yet stumble on relative position, layout, and counting. The team argues the failure ties to design choices, not just missing data. Prime suspects are CLIP-style encoders and the flattening of each image into a 1D token sequence. Their controlled study inside the LLaVA framework swaps encoders and adds 2D positional encoding. Spatial gaps persist across all variants, though encoder objectives and positional structure shape the behavior.
arxiv-2603-12945: Pandora Dominiak and co-authors weigh the supermassive black hole in the galaxy NGC 1387 from molecular gas motion. ALMA maps of carbon monoxide emission show a face-on disc in regular rotation. The disc has a central dip just past the black hole sphere of influence. Bayesian forward modeling with the Kinematic Molecular Simulation code fits the data cube. Hubble data pin down the stellar pull on the gas. The inferred mass fits the known mass-dispersion relation for such galaxies.
arxiv-2603-13245: Lars Malmqvist and Robin Barber describe an AI system that handles city planning documents in the UK. Planning law gives the public access to application files, but data law guards personal details. Staff now resolve that clash by hand, at high cost and legal risk. The system finds and redacts personal data, pulls key metadata, and checks drawings for set features. Officers approve each step inside their own software before any action is committed. Pilots at four councils test the workflow and savings.
arxiv-2603-13545: Katherine Elkins names and analyzes the AI Fiction Paradox in AI development. Developers treat large corpora of modern books as worth major cost and legal risk, yet models still struggle to write compelling long-form fiction. Elkins gives three challenges that explain why fiction resists AI generation. Narrative causation demands plot events that feel surprising yet retrospectively inevitable. Informational revaluation asks that early details gain new meaning later. Multi-scale emotional architecture is the third challenge she sets out.
arxiv-2603-14045: Zarrinkia, Srinivasan, and Thomo show that weak reasoning, not weak retrieval, is the main bottleneck in Graph-RAG question answering. In tests of the KET-RAG system, the gold answer sits in the retrieved context for most questions, yet final accuracy lags far behind. Most errors trace to reasoning slips. Two fixes help: SPARQL-style chain-of-thought prompts and graph-walk compression of the context. With both, a small open Llama model matches a much larger baseline at about one twelfth of the cost.
arxiv-2603-14145: Goel and co-authors introduce MMOU, a benchmark for joint sight, sound, and text reasoning in long real-world videos. It holds 20,000 hand-checked questions over 11,877 web videos across many domains. Thirteen core skills are tested, all needing facts merged across modes and time. More than twenty top multimodal models are evaluated. The best closed model scores only about 64 percent, and the best open one about 47 percent, which shows how far such systems still have to go.
arxiv-2603-14445: Xie and co-authors tackle committee setup for parallel Byzantine consensus in trusted hardware. Splitting nodes into small committees speeds consensus but weakens safety. Trusted execution environments restore safety, yet random committee picks can slow the system. The team builds an optimization model based on mixed integer programming. It weighs communication delays and node failure rates to cut transaction latency. Tests on Microsoft virtual machines show throughput gains of 15% in normal runs and 21% in fallback runs, the authors report.
arxiv-2603-14545: Kalantre and co-authors probe a spin liquid candidate with microwave resonance. The material is TbInO3, grown as epitaxial thin films. Frustration and quantum effects can block magnetic order in such systems. The films are too small for standard bulk probes. The team adapts circuit quantum electrodynamics tools with coplanar resonators. In-plane response shows strong frustration of order down to 20 millikelvin. That floor sits far below the Curie-Weiss energy scale. A crystal field study helps pin down the ground state.
arxiv-2603-14945: Weymouth fixes linear Kelvin wave theory at the surface limit with a modified kernel. Linear theory prices ship wakes cheaply versus viscous solvers. The classic Kelvin Green function blows up in energy as depth vanishes. An elliptic spanwise line integral reshapes the kernel here. Wave energy then stays finite across the whole free surface. Contour deformation speeds both point and line kernel scores hugely. Speedups of four to five orders of magnitude are reported. Wake shapes and resistance trends stay physical at zero depth.
arxiv-2603-15045: Schmitt and co-authors compare two ways to use large language models for speech recognition. One fuses a separate language model loosely with an acoustic model, called shallow fusion. The other builds the language model tightly into the recognizer. They test label units, model sizes, and attention interfaces on LibriSpeech and Loquacious. Shallow fusion wins on in-domain data at every size. The integrated model does better on the mixed HuggingFace leaderboard, mostly on out-of-domain speech.
arxiv-2603-15145: Huisman derives the moment of inertia tensor of an oloid, a smooth three-dimensional shape with uniform density. An oloid is the convex hull of two unit circles that lie in perpendicular planes. Each circle passes through the center of the other. He obtains an analytical expression for the full tensor. Numerical checks confirm the formula. The result gives the exact rotational inertia of this classic rolling shape.
arxiv-2603-15245: Kumar and co-authors test whether practicing with language models makes people better at empathic communication. Their platform pairs participants with a model that voices realistic troubles. A randomized study gathered about 34,000 messages from 968 participants. People reported feeling empathy but often failed to show it in words. Personalized coaching feedback from the model raised expressed empathy a lot, without making replies sound alike. The team also built a data-driven taxonomy of empathic phrases used in personal and workplace troubles.
arxiv-2603-15345: Dong and co-authors develop Pogorelov interior estimates for equations built from sums of Hessian operators of mixed orders. Their approach exploits the concavity of the summed operators. Under a dynamic semi-convexity condition, they derive the desired estimates. When the top order is n minus one or n, the condition drops away, which makes those estimates optimal. As a payoff, every whole-space admissible solution with quadratic growth and unit right-hand side must be a quadratic polynomial.
arxiv-2603-15545: Costilla and co-authors extend the Thiele equation to spin-transfer torque on curved surfaces, adding the Zhang-Li term. Curvature shapes the stability and motion of magnetic textures, but flat-space tools miss its effects. Their formalism reveals a direct coupling between current and curvature. That coupling appears as a gyrovector and an extra dissipative tensor. Applied to a skyrmion in a nanotube with varied curvature, the model yields an added Hall effect. It also generalizes the Walker limit condition.
arxiv-2603-15645: Ao proposes XLinear, a small neural forecaster built for long-range time series. Plain MLP forecasters resist noise well but miss long-range links. XLinear first splits a series into trend and seasonal parts. For the trend part, Enhanced Frequency Attention works in the frequency domain. For the seasonal part, a CrossFilter block guards noise robustness. The author reports state-of-the-art scores on test datasets. The model stays light while beating other MLP forecasters on long-range skill.
arxiv-2603-15845: Dombowsky, Engelhardt, and Ramdas build valid test values for unnormalized models. Such models name shapes but hide their normalizing constants. Likelihood ratio tests then break down in practice. Their fix borrows the parallel Besag-Clifford sampling trick. It yields samples exchangeable with data under the null claim. Valid e-values follow for any run length or step count. The values prove near log-optimal as sample counts grow. Averaging chains keeps validity and adds power. Galaxy velocity data test the method in action.
arxiv-2603-15945: Cao and Radenkovic grade delay-tolerant routing for a stadium quake scenario. The scene rebuilds the 2016 Central Italy quake during a Pescara match. Fans, responders, sensors, and vehicles form a patchy mobile network. Two protocols face identical simulation settings head to head. Epidemic routing floods copies through every contact it meets. Spray and Wait caps copies and waits for direct delivery chances. Delivery odds, latency, overhead, hops, and drops form the scorecard. Spray and Wait won on balance, with higher delivery and lower overhead.
arxiv-2603-16045: Shim and co-authors polish user prompts on the device itself to lift small model accuracy. Phone-grade models stumble on typos, vague asks, and missing context. Cloud prompt optimizers write long rule sheets that waste small context windows. Their POaaS layer routes each query to light specialist editors. A Cleaner, a Paraphraser, and a Fact-Adder each make minimal edits. Strict drift and length caps merge the edits safely. Clean prompts skip the layer under a cautious rule. Tests on two Llama models show accuracy and factuality gains.
arxiv-2603-16345: Camilleri and co-authors tune the fast radio burst search at the Northern Cross telescope. Pipelines must run in real time yet stay sensitive to brief bursts. Key settings are often picked by rule of thumb. The team built a test rig that injects fake bursts into realistic data. They swept settings for the Heimdall pipeline across a grid. One configuration recovered bursts well while beating real-time speed. The method should transfer to similar telescopes.
arxiv-2603-16445: Yang and co-authors show that images can warp moral judgment in vision-language models. Safety tuning works well in text, but visual inputs may bypass it. Their Moral Dilemma Simulation benchmark varies image and context separately. It rests on Moral Foundation Theory. Tests find that vision triggers fast, intuition-like paths. These override the slower, safer reasoning seen in text-only chats. The results expose a gap in multimodal safety alignment.
arxiv-2603-17145: Zhang and co-authors present REAL, a reinforcement learning method for training language models that judge with numeric scores. Standard RL uses binary rewards, which ignore how close a score is. A guess of 4 beats a guess of 1 when the truth is 5, and binary rewards miss that. REAL optimizes regression rewards directly, using a generalized policy gradient estimator. Training splits into exploring reasoning paths and refining the final score. Across model scales, REAL beat supervised and standard RL baselines.
arxiv-2603-17345: Huang, Kakimura, Kobayashi, and Terao study kernelization for weighted d-matroid intersection, a hard matching-style problem. A kernel shrinks an instance while keeping its key structure. They prove a polynomial kernel when one matroid is general and the rest are partition matroids. The size nearly matches the best known bound for d-dimensional matching. Their reachability idea also yields streaming algorithms and faster approximation schemes, they report.
arxiv-2603-17845: Archit and Pape re-test foundation models for cell instance segmentation in microscopy. Most cell tools extend the Segment Anything Model for lab images. Their study scores cell-specific and general models across cells, nuclei, and organoids. A new trick, automatic prompt generation, feeds SAM-style models better prompts. It lifts the micro-SAM base in test after test, they report. The tuned setup rivals the top CellPoseSAM model. Lessons guide future microscopy adaptations.
arxiv-2603-18245: Chen and co-authors present SafeAudit, a meta-audit framework for LLM agent tool-call safety. Benchmarks test many settings, but their coverage of unsafe tool patterns is unclear. An LLM enumerator builds test cases by listing valid tool workflows and user scenarios. A rule-resistance metric distills compact rules from benchmarks and finds gaps under them. Across 3 benchmarks and 12 environments, over 20% residual unsafe behaviors surfaced.
arxiv-2603-18445: Zeng and co-authors study exciton pairing across a gap in two-dimensional strongly linked semimetals. Top candidate materials share d-shell electrons with strong on-site Coulomb forces. Mean-field dynamics plus Monte Carlo runs cover Hubbard models with two and three orbitals. The on-site force cuts the pairing temperature hard, more so when pair density runs high. Rival pairing paths in the three-orbital case cut it more, and one path picks a single orbital.
arxiv-2603-18845: Seyboldt, Carlson, and Carpenter improve Hamiltonian Monte Carlo by picking better preconditioners. HMC scales well with dimension, but target curvature sets a large constant cost. Standard practice estimates variance from warmup draws, which converges slowly. Their estimator instead shrinks the Fisher divergence between a linearly reshaped density and a standard normal. Three forms are offered: diagonal, dense, and low-rank plus diagonal. On 114 models from posteriordb, the diagonal form beats Stan and PyMC defaults by a median factor of 1.3. The low-rank form wins by a median factor of 4.
arxiv-2603-18945: Joseph and co-authors argue that online ideology cannot be captured by one left-right line. That single scale hides views tied to race, climate, gender, and other fields. Their frame treats ideology as a layered network of social and mental links. It shows how ideology shows up in posts next to framing and related acts. It also makes a case for studying values and beliefs together. They show one way to run the frame on real data, though the work stays mainly a theory piece.
arxiv-2603-19045: Dong and Zhang prove a second-order bound for a class of equations on Hermitian manifolds. The equations involve sums of Hessian operators. The bound applies ahead of solving, to solutions that meet a dynamic plurisubharmonic condition. Such bounds are a key step toward showing that smooth solutions exist and behave well. The proof rests on a concavity inequality for complex sum-of-Hessian operators. That tool lets them control the second derivatives of admissible solutions across the compact manifold in a uniform way.
arxiv-2603-19845: Pereda studies how friendships form among 3,395 students, using an explainable boosting model. The model predicts whether a tie is positive or negative. Inputs cover traits like prosociality, reflection skill, and gender, plus triadic influence from the local network. Triadic influence dominates the predictions by a wide margin. Traits matter most for a small share of ties, about 0.24 percent. Those ties tend to be weaker, more often negative, and less balanced. The results support a layered view of tie formation.
arxiv-2603-20245: Toporensky and Zaslavskii find particle collisions of unbounded energy deep inside a charged black hole. The setting is the R region under the Cauchy horizon of the Reissner-Nordström metric. In their scenario, the center of mass energy grows without limit. Unlike classic high energy collision setups near black holes, no fine tuning of particle parameters is needed. The effect mirrors wave processes that destabilize the inner horizon. It serves as a massive particle counterpart to those wave effects.
arxiv-2603-20445: Roth and co-authors report a strikingly high methane D/H ratio in interstellar object 3I/ATLAS. The team measured near-infrared spectra of its coma with the Webb telescope. Methane D/H came out at 3.33 percent, with small error bars. That exceeds every methane value measured in the solar system. It is about 14 times the ratio in comet 67P. Deuteration in organics also outruns that in water, matching known trends. The enriched ratio hints the ices formed in a cold, metal-poor setting.
arxiv-2603-20645: Zhang and co-authors build theory for diffusion models on data that lies on a manifold. Real data often sits on a low dimensional curved surface. They model samples as points from a smooth Riemannian manifold. Their study splits the score function into parts by noise level. Curvature of the manifold shapes these parts in clear ways. A network design follows, with rates for score and distribution learning. The rates depend on the true dimension and curvature, not the ambient size.
arxiv-2603-20845: Ciardelli and Kontinen settle two long open questions about inquisitive first order logic. This logic extends classical logic with formulas that pose first order questions. One question asked if the logic is compact. Compactness means each consequence follows from finitely many premises. The other asked if its validities can be listed by a recursive system. They prove the answer to both is no. The logic also fails Craig interpolation, a hallmark of first order logic. Results extend to inquisitive team logic as well.
arxiv-2603-21145: Ye and co-authors present NeSy-Edge, a neuro-symbolic framework for self-healing across the computing continuum. Modern AI services run from cloud to edge devices, where scale and mixed hardware make resilience hard. Their edge-first design does local perception and reasoning on a small edge node. Raw logs become structured events, then feed a sparse symbolic causal graph. Causal evidence joins past troubleshooting knowledge for root-cause analysis. A cloud model is called only at the final diagnosis stage. Tests under heavy log noise stay robust.
arxiv-2603-21345: Branquinho and co-authors build the bidiagonal factorization of banded recursion matrices for mixed-type multiple orthogonal polynomials. The banded matrix comes from a Gauss-Borel factorization of a moment matrix. Their work writes it as a product of lower and upper bidiagonal factors. The factors come from Christoffel transforms of the moment matrix, as quotients of Gauss-Borel factors of perturbed matrices. They give explicit formulas for the entries in terms of tau-determinants. The theory is then applied to multiple Hahn polynomials.
arxiv-2603-21645: Moradi and co-authors study sequences made by automata that read numbers in the Zeckendorf, or Fibonacci, form. They build automata that accept basic arithmetic relations in that form. For each build, they count the states it needs. They also track how basic operations on such sequences change the state count. One result sharpens a bound from a recent paper by Bosma and Don. They also weigh the cost of using Büchi arithmetic in practice to build some of these machines.
arxiv-2603-21845: Colom i Bernadich and co-authors hunt for millisecond pulsars in the globular cluster Omega Centauri with MeerKAT and Parkes data. They ran acceleration and jerk searches and timed pulsars across 2021 to 2025. One new isolated pulsar turned up, spinning every 4.538 milliseconds. Timing refined the orbits of all known binaries, with big changes for 3 systems. Several pulsars look like black widows, and one wide pair shows an eccentric orbit. Spin-down rates point to the cluster's gravity well, and any central black hole must weigh under 100,000 suns.
arxiv-2603-22245: Yakymenko and co-authors encode DNA sequences as quantum states using rotary position embeddings. The encoding makes edit distance track the overlap between quantum states. On the classical side, the same idea yields RotorMap, a GPU mapping tool. Tests on human and maize genomes show speedups of 50 to 700 times over Minimap2. For quantum hardware, their Angular encoding outputs state preparation circuits directly. They run tests on Quantinuum machines, up to the 98-qubit Helios-1. One use they propose is quantum DNA authentication.
arxiv-2603-22345: Meng and co-authors recognize emotions in conversations from text, audio, and images at once. Graph networks help by modeling how speakers depend on each other. Most methods fuse the modalities with fixed settings. That forces one balance across all emotion types. Their model, DF-GCN, lets the fusion shift for each utterance. Ordinary differential equations inside the graph net capture how emotional links evolve. Prompts from a global utterance vector guide the fusion. Tests on two public datasets show gains over prior methods.
arxiv-2603-22645: Sanjeevappa, Chandrasekaran, and Betouras study triplet superconductivity near a special band feature. The feature is a high-order Van Hove singularity of X9 type at the Fermi energy. It sits in a four-fold symmetric dispersion for a quantum material. The authors first detail its form and density of states. They then add Hubbard repulsion and solve the gap equation. A triplet state can form, with critical temperature following a power law in interaction strength. They also bound the possible critical temperature for the ruthenate Sr3Ru2O7.
arxiv-2603-22945: Jones, da Cunha, and Battisti test how well the MAGPHYS model recovers galaxy traits. They fit synthetic spectra for about thirty-one thousand simulated star-forming galaxies from EAGLE. True values are known, so accuracy can be checked directly. Under ideal sampling, mass, star formation rate, and dust traits come back close to truth. Mass-weighted ages do not. Wrong assumptions about star formation history bias mass estimates, they find. In realistic survey data, dust traits degrade without far-infrared coverage.
arxiv-2603-23245: Han and six co-authors test neural differential equation models for model-based reinforcement learning. Neural stochastic equations capture random transition dynamics better than plain neural ODEs. That edge yields strong policies with fewer samples in hard settings. The team also adapts policies to changed dynamics through inverse models, using few new interactions. For partly observed tasks, they build a latent model that mixes an ODE with a GAN-trained random part. Policies from that model match or beat leading model-based and model-free baselines.
arxiv-2603-23345: Sun and six co-authors present FHAvatar, a system that builds 3D head avatars from a few casual photos. Older tools need dense photo sets or slow per-person fitting. FHAvatar splits face and hair apart in texture space. Planar Gaussians carry the face, while strand-based Gaussians carry the hair. A transformer backbone learns cross-view priors from many heads, then fuses the few new shots fast. New avatars reach top quality within minutes. They support live animation, hairstyle swaps, and stylized edits.
arxiv-2603-23645: Vergara studies truncated bilinear forms built from synchronized kernels. A one-dimensional kernel sets the singularity, while two phase maps carry the geometry. His scheme runs in three moves: reduction, analytic transfer, and geometric recomposition. The reduction works at the level of pushforward measures in the level variable. Control of the pushforward densities then feeds estimates back to the problem. As a first case, he moves a sparse domination rule into this setting. Two regimes split apart: a uniform one and a critical one near phase folds.
arxiv-2603-23845: Kim and co-authors present 3D-LLDM, a model that makes synthetic liver MRI scans with matching masks. Labeled medical scans are scarce, which slows training of analysis tools. Their latent diffusion model is guided by labels for the liver, veins, and tumors. It trains on 720 real clinical scans from Samsung Medical Center. Its image quality score beats GANs by 70.9 percent and diffusion baselines by 26.7 percent. Added synthetic scans lift tumor segmentation scores across five network designs.
arxiv-2603-23945: Malter links conic modules to line bundles on toric stacks, to ease work on non-commutative resolutions. Faber, Muller, and Smith built such resolutions from complete sums of conic modules. The new viewpoint cuts the combinatorial cost of these objects. Malter gives exact conditions for when an incomplete sum yields a resolution of a toric algebra. He also shows the check can be reduced to the case with no torsion in the class group. He classifies almost simplicial Gorenstein cones as a final case.
arxiv-2603-24645: Amaral and co-authors propose GravNet, a global detector network for high-frequency gravitational waves. Such waves, in the megahertz to gigahertz range, could come from phenomena tied to deep cosmology questions. A single detector can hardly split a real signal from device or background noise. GravNet instead correlates signals from devices at far-apart sites, boosting detection and revealing the signal's nature. The design targets cavities in strong magnetic fields, and a first demo experiment is described.
arxiv-2603-25545: Appleby and Pal sort the long-run fates of solutions to forced second-order linear equations. The unforced system settles to zero, but a forcing term can shake that calm. They give a full test for three fates: the solution fades to zero, it stays bounded without settling, or it runs off without bound. Wild cases exist: forcing can oscillate fast and grow, yet the solution still dies away. Its slopes, though, may blow up on the way. The tests draw a clean map of the border cases.
arxiv-2603-25645: Hamdi, Yang, and Gao introduce Colon-Bench, a benchmark for lesion annotation in colonoscopy videos. Dense labels for full procedures are scarce, which slows AI work here. Their workflow joins temporal proposals, box tracking, AI visual checks, and human review. The dataset covers 528 videos and 14 lesion types. It holds over 300,000 boxes, 213,000 masks, and 133,000 words of clinical text. The authors test leading multimodal models on classification, segmentation, and question answering. They also propose a prompting strategy that lifts zero-shot scores.
arxiv-2603-25745: Lao and co-authors present LGTM, a feed-forward method for 3D Gaussian splatting at 4K resolution. Older methods place one primitive per pixel, so counts grow fast with resolution. That makes 4K output impractical. LGTM predicts a compact set of Gaussians instead. Each Gaussian carries its own texture. This splits surface complexity from rendering resolution. The result is high-quality 4K novel view synthesis with no per-scene tuning. The authors report that it uses far fewer primitives than pixel-aligned methods.
arxiv-2603-25845: Motta reports simulations of light paths that form and vanish inside photonic crystals. The crystals are two-dimensional silicon waveguides that fluids can infiltrate. Filling selected holes reshapes which routes light can take. Analysis separates bandgap narrowing from defect-mode weakening. Defect weakening dominates, decaying transmission 2.4 times faster at the tested indices. The fill pattern steers signals, with an L-bend selectivity of 0.98. A feedback model yields self-organized paths that reach 63 percent of a hand-designed guide's transmission.
arxiv-2603-26045: Yocam, Vaidyan, and Wang map the hidden dimensions inside language models that drive hallucination. A simple probe on last-token states finds a small set of high-variance dimensions. They call these hallucination nodes, or H-Nodes. The probe reaches an AUC of 0.90 across four model families. An attack that boosts these nodes at run time steers output with little visibility. Their defense cancels the excess in the same pass. It cuts grounded drift by 33 to 42 percent over static cancellation. General skill stays nearly intact.
arxiv-2603-26445: Huang and co-authors examine the surface of a high entropy alloy at the nanoscale with nano-infrared tools. They study a one-micrometre film using hyperspectral imaging and single-point spectra across the 700 to 1700 wavenumber range. The probe resolves detail down to the 20 nanometre tip size, whatever the light wavelength. The CuPdAgPtAu alloy shows stronger absorption and reflection in one band, matching Drude-Lorenz models yet also hinting at oxide growth. The team also models how polarisation could extend the method to full 3D surface analysis.
arxiv-2603-26545: Kiuru computes QED scattering cross sections in magnetic fields stronger than the Schwinger limit. Past that limit, quantum electrodynamics turns nonlinear, as in the skies of magnetars. He adapts a formalism first used for magnetic catalysis. The work covers all tree-level one-to-two, two-to-one, and two-to-two processes without a photon propagator. Results are coded into an open-source Python package for reuse. A companion letter takes up what the new cross sections mean for magnetar plasma behaviour.
arxiv-2603-27445: Sharma and co-authors simulate how a swimming bacterium moves through mucus. Such fluids mix springy polymers with tiny pores. The cell body is much larger than its tail bundle. Their two-fluid model lets the tail push the solvent. Drag links the solvent and polymer parts. A slender-body method handles the thin tail forces. Key flow parts can be computed in advance. That split speeds each run a great deal. The setup yields swimming speeds for real shapes.
arxiv-2603-27945: Li and Yu propose a general way to pump spin supercurrents. Andreev reflection turns charge current into supercurrent in metals. Spin conservation suggests a twin effect in triplet superconductors. A spin torque scales with the triplet order parameter. It converts particle spin into Cooper pair spin. A nearby magnet with moving magnetization drives the flow. The scheme works even without equilibrium pair polarization. Particle-hole symmetry lifts efficiency past standard spin pumping.
arxiv-2603-28445: Barkatou and El Morsalani study a return map built from the boundary of a convex body and a thickness function. Rays shoot out to an outer boundary and back, defining a discrete motion on the inner surface. The authors expand the map locally and show curvature shapes how thickness changes steer it. Fixed points match the thickness function's critical points. A linearization at those points sorts stable from unstable cases. Tests on the unit circle confirm the theory.
arxiv-2603-28845: Ichikawa and co-authors present OneComp, an open source tool that compresses generative AI models in one line. Big models face limits from memory size, latency, and hardware cost. Compression cuts parameter precision, but the workflow is fragmented and expert heavy. Given a model name and the hardware at hand, OneComp inspects the model on its own. It plans mixed precision steps and runs staged quantization, from layer wise to global refinement. The first checkpoint is deployable, and later stages improve the same model.
arxiv-2603-29345: De Gibert and de Gibert give the first broad review of open machine translation for Esperanto. Esperanto is a constructed language with regular grammar. It has rich online resources but little modern translation study. They compare rule-based systems, encoder-decoder models, and language models of many sizes. Six language directions link English, Spanish, Catalan, and Esperanto. Scores come from automatic metrics and human judges. The NLLB family won every language pair. Trained compact models and a fine-tuned language model came close.
arxiv-2603-29545: Hughes and co-authors examine how generative AI tools are reshaping cybercrime. Dire forecasts picture rogue agents seizing key infrastructure. Their analysis, using innovation theory, paints a calmer picture. They coin two bounding cases: a Stand-Alone Complex of boxed gang solutions, and low-end Vibercrime from vibe coding. Early underground data show modest uptake so far. AI helps with passive income schemes and simple fraud, mostly for skilled actors. Low-skill users gain little from vibe coding tools. Social learning still drives how newcomers enter.
arxiv-2603-29745: Vater and co-authors model changing magnetic fields inside ferrite parts, work driven by the MagNet Challenge 2025. Good forecasts must track time and heat to help design magnetic parts. They compare model types with varying amounts of built-in physics. A plain gated recurrent unit with careful starting values wins on size versus accuracy. With just 325 parameters per material, it scores 8.02 percent sequence error. That model took first place in its challenge class.
arxiv-2603-29845: Zhang and co-authors run a reproducibility study of generative recommenders under cold-start conditions. New users and new items both lack interaction history. Language-model recommenders are often expected to help via item text and test-time context. Yet cold-start is rarely the main test setting in past work. Design choices also tend to change together, muddying reported gains. Their study uses one unified suite of cold-start protocols. It aims to make such gains readable at last.
arxiv-2604-00245: Pons and Le Mogne study triangular Dyck paths from Bergeron and Mazin through (q,t)-enumeration, introducing triangular and sim-sym tableaux plus a deficit statistic that reinterprets the dinv. They use it to prove new results on triangular 2-partitions and to state a conjecture on (q,t,r)-enumeration for a certain lattice interval. The deficit statistic is the paper's key new tool, linking the tableaux to the enumeration counts.
arxiv-2604-00745: Raghuram and colleagues build a one-dimensional synthetic lattice from rotational states of ultracold RbCs molecules to study the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model. Light probes and time tests after state setup show long coherence times, about 500 times the lattice step period, across 8 turning states. Reading each site on its own lets them test how chiral and non-chiral knocks affect the edge states that topology shields.
arxiv-2604-01045: Endo, Iwaki, and Pajitnov construct an endless family of new Cappell-Shaneson knot pairs, plus cases with the same Alexander poly that are unmatched. It is well known that for m at least 2, at most two distinct m-knots share a matching outside, and such a pair is called non-mirror. Finding all sizes where such pairs exist is an old knot theory problem. Cappell and Shaneson gave a method in 1976 for building non-mirror knot pairs, and this paper builds new cases with their method.
arxiv-2604-01145: Caceres and eight colleagues outline FerBo, a superconducting circuit built to resist two kinds of quantum noise across a wide, reachable range of settings. It pairs a large coil with a small capacitor and a highly transmitting Josephson weak link. Mixing the fermionic Andreev states in that link with the circuit's own electromagnetic mode guards against energy loss, while spread-out wave patterns, as in the fluxonium qubit, guard against phase drift.
arxiv-2604-01345: Krishnamurthy and Snow tackle adaptive inverse reinforcement learning, where a watcher rebuilds a learner's hidden loss function from its gradients. The snag: the needed gradients are counterfactual, tied to events of zero chance along the learner's path. Naive Monte Carlo sampling is far too wasteful, and kernel smoothing is slow. They recast the setup as a ratio of plain averages from Malliavin calculus quantities, restoring standard estimation rates. They derive the needed Malliavin derivatives and adjoint Skorohod integrals for a general Langevin setup, plus a concrete method using them.
arxiv-2604-01545: Yu and colleagues study representation autoencoders within continuous step-by-step sequence models, called RAE-AR. They spot two blocks: hard per-token spread modeling and the train-test gap, known as exposure bias. They ease modeling with token simplification via spread normalization, which helps fit. They add Gaussian noise in training to fight exposure bias. Their tweaks close the gap, letting them match classic VAEs on sequence models.
arxiv-2604-01645: Fleischer and colleagues present GONDAR, a sink-centric fuzzing method for Java vulnerability finding. GONDAR first identifies reachable and exploitable sink call sites through CWE scanning and LLM static filtering. It deploys two agents working with a guided fuzzer. An exploration agent generates inputs to reach target call sites by solving path constraints. An exploitation agent synthesizes proof-of-concept exploits from vulnerability-triggering conditions. Agents and fuzzer exchange seeds and runtime feedback. On real-world Java benchmarks, GONDAR discovers four times more vulnerabilities than Jazzer, the top Java fuzzer.
arxiv-2604-02045: Boizard and colleagues turn causal language models into bidirectional encoders with open source BidirLM. Conversions lack agreed objectives, suffer catastrophic forgetting at scale, and cannot absorb generative models. Ablations on Gemma3 and Qwen3 find an omitted masking phase critical to adaptation. A dual plan scales the process without pretraining data, combining weight merging with a light data mixture that limits it. Merging the encoders with causal models transfers strengths, and the five beat alternatives on text, vision and audio benchmarks.
arxiv-2604-02145: Jeong measures AI agent temperament from behavior, not self report. His Model Temperament Index scores reactivity, compliance, sociality and resilience through structured exams that separate what a model can do from how it tends to act. Profiling ten small models, he finds the four axes largely independent, compliance splitting into formal and stance facets, and temperament unrelated to model size. Alignment, he shows, reshapes temperament by creating facet splits absent in base models.
arxiv-2604-02445: Yeh details an open source Matrix Profile benchmark entry for time series anomaly detection on TSB-AD. The system joins pre sorted sums, exclusion zone aware neighbor lookup for repeat events, and moving average smoothing. Open code details, settings for single and multi tracks, and benchmark results serve as a guide for Matrix Profile anomaly work. Analysis covers overall board scores and trends across data.
arxiv-2604-02545: Barla and de Berardinis turn competency questions, normally used to check a knowledge graph at design time, into run-time plans for storytelling about intangible cultural heritage. Their neuro-symbolic system plans, retrieves and generates from a knowledge graph, keeping every story evidence-closed and auditable. Tested on a new Live Aid knowledge graph, the study weighs symbolic, hybrid and graph-based retrieval against each other on precision, richness and coherence.
arxiv-2604-02945: Yang and six colleagues propose MSAO, an adaptive modality sparsity-aware offloading framework with edge-cloud collaboration for efficient multimodal language model inference. The system targets small edge devices. A lightweight module computes an activation sparsity metric through space-time-modal analysis. An edge-cloud scheduler shifts workloads by those scores and live system states to hide communication latency. Tests show latency down 30 percent, overhead down 30 to 65 percent, and throughput up by half to more than double.
arxiv-2604-03345: Khalid and colleagues work out how to count the chip cost of Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks on any platform. Rather than chip metrics that need a full hardware build, their counts use real multiplications, bit operations, and additions with bit-shifts, all read straight from network structure. The study covers B-spline, Gaussian radial basis function, Chebyshev, and Fourier variants, allowing fair comparison across networks.
arxiv-2604-03845: Mauricio Corrêa and Simone Noja studied cohomology classes that vanish off a closed subset, whose supported lifts form a torsor. In plain terms, they pinned down when a supported lift is unique and how its ambiguity is shaped. They tracked that torsor under excision, base change, proper pushforward with trace data, and external products. Under purity and orientation hypotheses, its translation group matches a Gysin image inside the Euler-class kernel. A stable categorical enhancement links the torsor to nullhomotopy spaces, with Milnor torsors for characteristic-class defects.
arxiv-2604-04045: Islem Khemissi and team built SmartPatchLinker, a browser tool that shows up meaning-linked code changes during review. In large code repos, related patches often show up days late, doubling effort and slowing reviews. The Chrome add-on with a local AI backend plugs into Gerrit, ranking linked changes with trust marks when a patch is opened. Value and ease-of-use tests studied how the tool supports review teams in their workflow.
arxiv-2604-04345: Zhou and colleagues explore underapproximation ideas from program logics, which reason about reach rather than safety, inside a type and effect system. The team uses underapproximate type specifications to guide building of test generators probing systems. A key novelty is catching underapproximate acts with symbolic traces showing data and control links. They build the approach in Clouseau, testing it by plugging generators into property-based testing frameworks like QCheck and model-checking tools like P. In both settings, Clouseau's generators beat the default plan and rival hand-made solutions.
arxiv-2604-04545: Kristjansen and colleagues study gate control for Ringkoebing Fjord, a Danish basin separated from the North Sea by flow gates. Operators decide when and how many gates to open or close. They balance conflicting safety and performance requirements: holding water in range, allowing traffic and fish migration. Using a digital twin with sea-level and wind forecasts, the team learns a gate controller online. Tested under normal tides, high waters and low waters, the controllers satisfy safety requirements, unlike a baseline, while performing similarly on other requirements.
arxiv-2604-05045: Lade and four co-authors propose PCA-Triage, a streaming algorithm for multi-channel sensor networks in industrial IoT that often exceed available bandwidth. It converts incremental PCA loadings into proportional per-channel sampling rates under a bandwidth budget, running with zero trainable parameters and under a millisecond per decision. Evaluated on seven benchmarks against nine baselines, it is the best unsupervised method on three of six datasets at half bandwidth. On TEP, it achieves an F1 of 0.961, within a tenth of a percent of full-data performance.
arxiv-2604-05145: Dessart and six co-authors model the photospheric phase of supernova SN2023ixf, a Type II supernova interacting with material, using nonlocal equilibrium time-dependent radiative-transfer calculations. The calculations cover 20 to 120 days and span ultraviolet to infrared. The explosion of a 15 solar mass star with mass loss during the phase yields ejecta of 7 to 8 solar masses. It yields a kinetic energy of 1.2e51 erg and a nickel mass of five hundredths solar masses. That model matches the photospheric duration and brightness, with circumstellar interaction shaping later evolution.
arxiv-2604-05345: Adeseye, Isoaho, Virtanen, and Tahir build a profiler that rates how expert a speaker sounds from spoken answers. It sorts replies into Novice, Basic, Advanced, or Expert, so machines can match their tone to the person in front of them. Its layered design runs on a small open language model and scores each answer as it arrives. Tested on 82 recorded transcripts and 402 live interviews, its ratings matched speakers' own ratings in 83 to 97 percent of cases, with gaps traced to self-rating bias and unclear answers.
arxiv-2604-05545: Li and three colleagues generate spatial room impulse responses in real time for virtual-reality sound. Their multimodal model takes scene data plus low-order reflections computed by geometrical acoustics, then predicts full responses that plug into personalized head-related transfer functions. A new multi-scene dataset supports the model, which tests ahead of rivals on performance.
arxiv-2604-05645: Dallant and Kozma improve the space-time tradeoff for exact traveling salesman solving, beating every prior scheme for a wide parameter range. Sparse set systems with many maximal chains drive the gain, reaching a time-space product below 3.572. Along the way they disprove a 2013 conjecture of Johnson, Leader, and Russell, and extend the method to permutation problems over semirings.
arxiv-2604-06145: Ghosh, Maity, and Ullah revisit the sign of the equilateral bispectrum from a massive hidden-sector scalar exchanged during inflation. With only the leading boost-breaking interaction, that signal is always negative whatever the coupling sign. Adding the full effective-field-theory operators creates rival cubic terms that compete in that setup, so the sign stops being universal. The authors derive a critical ratio of couplings marking the boundary between positive and negative results, a boundary that slower sound speed and multi-particle exchange shift further.
arxiv-2604-06245: Fang and three colleagues reframe crater analysis as instance-level image retrieval, not detection alone. Their CraterBench-R benchmark holds 25,000 crater identities with multi-scale views and verified queries. Self-supervised Vision Transformers with in-domain pretraining dominate baselines, and keeping patch tokens for late-interaction matching beats single-vector pooling. They propose instance-token aggregation: select seed tokens, assign the rest by cosine similarity, and aggregate clusters. At 16 seeds it improves mean average precision by 17.9 points, and at 64 seeds it matches all-token accuracy with less storage.
arxiv-2604-06345: Miele, Morisi, Peinado, and Qamar treat type-I seesaw as low-scale seesaw via Casas-Ibarra. Here, radiative corrections can dominate the tree-level part, so Casas-Ibarra no longer fixes physical neutrino masses and mixings. They extend Casas-Ibarra to the loop-corrected equation, absorbing one-loop corrections into right-handed neutrino masses, so light neutrino masses match experiment. Right-handed neutrino processes, such as heavy neutral lepton searches, ignore one-loop corrections. Muon-to-electron-photon decay competitively constrains heavy neutral lepton searches above 100 GeV.
arxiv-2604-06445: Hu, Chen, and Zhu build a unified decomposition for stochastic block models. A plug-in estimate replaces the unknown probability matrix. That creates simple and composite perturbations, replacing the matrix in the numerator or both parts. The sum of squares splits into three parts, with a sharp split: the simple cross term fades; the composite one does not. The composite perturbation becomes two bias matrices plus the simple perturbation, isolating error sources. The largest eigenvalue statistic's condition hits the optimal rate, and the linear spectral statistic is proved asymptotically normal.
arxiv-2604-06645: Milesis and Salins prove that noisy reaction-diffusion systems with triangular mass control live for all time. Deterministic versions were already known to exist globally under quasipositivity, triangular mass control, and polynomial growth. Stochastic versions, however, had been studied under different reaction assumptions that excluded natural models like reversible chemical networks under mass-action law. The authors show that suitable multiplicative noise preserves global existence and uniqueness under the mass-control structure, settling an open question for chemistry and biology models.
arxiv-2604-06845: Zhong, Gao, and Wang give dialogue systems long-term memory with HingeMem. Existing approaches lean on summaries or OpenIE graphs with fixed retrieval, limiting adaptability and raising cost. HingeMem applies event segmentation theory, drawing boundaries when person, time, location, or topic changes and writing the segment as a hyperedge. Query-adaptive retrieval then decides what to fetch, routing over element-indexed memory, and how much to fetch, setting depth by query type. Tests on LOCOMO show about 20 percent relative improvement over baselines while cutting token cost by 68 percent against HippoRAG2.
arxiv-2604-07045: Souza and Mendes present a paper on tuning a new smart radio surface for links that serve many users at once. The beyond diagonal surface can bend radio waves in more ways than an older design, but its many settings are hard to pick well. The authors propose a depth first tree search that walks through setting choices step by step. Their tests show a good balance between strong signal links and modest computing cost.
arxiv-2604-07145: Hossen, Shah, and Guvenc design a coordination scheme for drone users in fifth generation macro networks, where drones suffer harsh, patchy interference. The trouble comes largely from side lobes of tilted base station antennas aimed at ground users, which leaves aerial users with uneven cover. Boosting chosen cells to help drones can worsen interference between cells, so the paper jointly tunes antenna tilt and time slot scheduling. The plan lifts the worst drone signal to interference ratio over a grid of drone spots while keeping ground users served.
arxiv-2604-07345: Vercellino and six colleagues measure how generative-AI workloads draw power, to help plan whole data-center facilities. Public power data is scarce and patchy, so they record training, fine-tuning, and inference jobs at tenth-of-a-second resolution on H100 GPUs, using standard MLCommons and vLLM benchmarks. The resulting profiles are released openly. Scaled up through a bottom-up, event-driven facility model, they produce realistic whole-facility energy curves for grid, generation, and microgrid planning.
arxiv-2604-07445: Cha and three colleagues map filaments in the merging cluster Abell 2744 with weak lensing. They pair global matched-filter scans with a new stepwise 2D tracing method for local directions. Filters find filaments to the northwest and east in inner and outer rings, but the eastern case stays unstable under a fixed reference point. Using its locally traced direction resolves the tension, and the filaments match diffuse X-ray structures and merger axes.
arxiv-2604-07545: Wang and ten colleagues build a phase-field model coupling charge transition levels to study grain edges in acceptor-doped oxides. Charge transition levels are Fermi levels where a defect changes charge state. They govern the bulk mix, while bending in space-charge layers induces extra charge-state shifts. The model holds multi-valent oxygen gaps, multivalent dopants, and free charges. It is applied to iron-doped strontium oxide across wide oxygen pressure and heat. Runs reveal slow and fast grain edge types during motion, in line with tests.
arxiv-2604-07645: Wang and Jiang introduce PRIME, a gradient-free learning tool for autonomous tool-use agents on long tasks with human users. Multi-turn interaction demands agents refine their grasp of user intent through talk, yet reinforcement learning costs heavily and struggles with turn-level credit. PRIME distills multi-turn trajectories into readable lessons across three zones: winning strategies, failure patterns, and user preferences. These lessons evolve and guide future behavior via retrieval-augmented generation. Across diverse user settings, PRIME matches gradient-based methods while keeping cost efficiency and clarity.
arxiv-2604-08045: Fati and 11 colleagues adapt foundation models for annotation-efficient adnexal mass segmentation in cine ultrasound images. Ultrasound checks of adnexal masses challenge doctors through varied reads and large observer spread. Machine segmentation supports number-based risk scoring, yet fully trained designs demand large pixel-level label sets and struggle with domain shifts. Their label-efficient system uses the meaning priors of a ready-made DINOv3 backbone with a Dense Prediction Transformer-style decoder. The decoder rebuilds multi-scale cues step by step, joining global meaning with fine detail.
arxiv-2604-08145: Predin introduces the Zitterbewegung areal rate operator linking trembling motion and band topology. Built from shaking between-band displacement and velocity, it distinguishes clockwise from leftward motion. For a generic gapped two-band model in 2D, the Zitterbewegung areal rate proves matched to Berry curvature. The proof uses only spectral maps and is therefore gauge-safe. It is a constant of motion at each point, although its shift and speed wobble in time. Its sign marks anticlockwise from rightward motion and matches the Berry curvature sign.
arxiv-2604-08345: Liu and Zhang revisit a claim about splitting indivisible goods fairly among people whose values take only two levels. They exhibit a case where an earlier fast method for a fair and efficient split can run forever without ending. Their replacement fast method finds a WEFX split, weighted envy free up to any good, that stays efficient, and the same approach also yields a weighted equitable split of that kind.
arxiv-2604-08745: Promyslov, Romanov, and Yurieva solve the Cramér-Lundberg ruin problem with claims and investment by share exactly. The survival chance equation reduces to a doubly confluent Heun equation, giving an exact solution in Heun functions. A verification theorem confirms the solution, and a broad analysis traces how ruin risk moves with the share invested. The short paper gives the exact solution, its proof, and its reading in terms of the share invested.
arxiv-2604-09045: Hsu and three colleagues bring label-free object-centric learning to 3D Gaussian splatting, the method behind lifelike 3D scenes. Current methods guide radiance fields with 2D masks from visual base models. But those signals are not object-based, and they demand cleanup or training to resolve mix-ups of the same object across views. Worse, what is learned sticks to one scene, blocking reuse. Their scene-free codebook enables object tracking and naming without per-scene fine-tuning, yielding tidy models and better transfer for robots and scene tasks.
arxiv-2604-09345: Xu gives a general recipe for spurion analysis in models whose choice rules come from order-free non-invertible fusion algebras. The build covers algebras with elements that need not mirror themselves. It tracks coupling constants step by step in any scattering events at tree and loop orders. The work unifies earlier near-group and Z-M over Z-2 studies, backing helper accounts using lifted Abelian groups with stated breaking terms.
arxiv-2604-09445: Omama, Berton, Foxlin, and Kim propose AsymLoc, asymmetric feature matching for efficient visual localization. Precise real-time visual localization matters for AR, VR, and robotics, especially on smart glasses. Many efficient models exist, but further compute cuts without accuracy loss remain essential for practical deployment. AsymLoc uses a large Teacher for database images offline and a lightweight Student for query images online, aligning Student to Teacher through geometry matching. That enables fast parameter-less nearest-neighbor matching, reaching up to 95 percent of teacher accuracy with much smaller models.
arxiv-2604-09545: Porto and Riva derive black-hole scattering results at fifth post-Newtonian order: impulse, scattering angle, and time delay, including radiation-reaction and hereditary effects. An isotropic-like picture, with energy and angular-momentum losses, fixes the two-body motion from scattering data. Feynman's prescription yields a universal term in the conservative Hamiltonian. It fixes Effective One Body coefficients in line with the Tutti-Frutti framework. A rival gamma-3 prescription agrees over the shared regime but gives an opposite-sign memory term at one order.
arxiv-2604-09745: Das derives a functional for kernel dynamics on graphs from the Maximum Caliber principle on the transfer function of the graph Laplacian eigenbasis. The stationarity condition decouples into N 1-D problems. It yields fixed-point kernels via exponential tilting, Fisher-Rao geodesics, and Hessian stability criterion. Spectral entropy supplies an order-N signal for phase transitions. Claims are verified on the path graph P8 with a mutual-information source using the kernelcal library. The work rests on an analogy with Einstein's field equations, a template, not an established equivalence.
arxiv-2604-09845: Jałowiczor and 20 co-authors present new spectroscopic data for a white dwarf and its two wide, co-moving companions. They confirm a hydrogen-rich DA white dwarf, with a temperature near 6,200 Kelvin and a mass of about three fifths of a solar mass, near average. Spectra in the near-infrared from the two stellar companions show the inner one is an M dwarf of spectral type M8. The outer companion looks like a possible M6 plus M9 binary. The paper examines evidence suggesting the system may be quadruple.
arxiv-2604-09945: Howard, Su, and Fraser study how large vision-language models judge a person's moral, ethical, and political values across cultural contexts in images. Using counterfactual sets showing the same person in different cultural settings, they pair moral-foundations and lexical analyses with a grounding check against two human surveys. Across 4.8 million model generations, they find three survey-grounding bias patterns repeating across diverse model architectures. Nationality grounding proves text-dominant, while image cues drive religion and socioeconomic grounding most, and image conditioning can amplify the bias patterns.
arxiv-2604-10345: Sun and colleagues study code change reasons and build a tool to recover them. They trace nine reason parts in 63 commits from five open-source Java projects. Seven parts appear, and reasons are highly split: commit notes and pull requests mainly hold GOAL, while issues and pull requests hold NEED and CHOICE more often. No single file type holds all parts, so cross-file work is needed. ARGUS finds GOAL, NEED, and CHOICE lines across a commit's files and builds reason notes, with about 51 percent hits and about 93 percent recall.
arxiv-2604-10545: Cao and eight colleagues shape self study chats with old ideas about knowledge. Learners often stall in deep talks and drown in tangled facts. Their CausaDisco tool weaves Aristotle's four causes into prompts that spawn apt follow ups. A first study of 26 learners mapped how knowledge views steer chat habits. A trial with 36 learners then found livelier talks, deeper probes, and wider angles than baseline chats.
arxiv-2604-10645: Cabot argues that vibe coding should not replace model-based engineering but join it. In vibe coding, language models turn plain-language requests into running code. Models have grown too complex to specify by hand, while vibe-coded output risks flaws, scaling trouble, and upkeep burdens. His vibe-driven model-based engineering blends the two, using models to steer AI generation toward reliable complex systems. He sketches the core concepts, the new development paths the blend opens, and its open challenges.
arxiv-2604-10745: Jang and three colleagues build the first large benchmark of diverse queries that mean the same thing, for adaptive retrieval-augmented generation, combining human-written and model-made rewrites. Adaptive RAG fetches text only when needed, but real queries vary in surface form with the same intent, and that impact was little studied. Judging answer quality, compute cost, and fetch choices, they find a critical weak spot: small surface changes sharply alter fetch behavior and accuracy. Larger models perform better, yet toughness does not improve accordingly.
arxiv-2604-11245: Majer and three colleagues add resource budgets to epistemic logic, where acquiring evidence costs time, memory, or energy. Their semiring-annotated topological spaces, called seats, extend Topological Evidence Logic by tagging evidence with the budgets sufficient to observe it. The framework reasons about what is affordable, not just what is observable in principle. The authors supply sound, strongly complete axiom systems plus notions of bisimulation and disjoint union to chart expressive power.
arxiv-2604-11545: Caprioglio and Berthouze show heterophily, preferring unlike partners, as a minimal local mechanism for self-organized synergy. In a spin-glass model with changing couplings, solving the three-unit case by hand reveals the mechanism. Heterophily weakens pairwise ties while inducing high-order ones through geometric limits on selected configurations. Simulations confirm the effect in large systems and under varied traits. Applied to opinions, heterophily disrupts splits while group forces explain opinions better than pairwise ones.
arxiv-2604-11745: Kim and three colleagues propose a data-driven oscillator model for multi-frequency turbulence. Phase-reduction simplifies wavy flows, but phase-based models usually handle only single-frequency flows given chaotic spectra. Their framework pulls key oscillators from flow data with custom autoencoders, then models oscillator motion with neural networks to predict such motion. Applied to supersonic flow over a cavity, oscillators from spanwise pressure show main large-scale features. With observation fixes, the model forecasts wavy motion well.
arxiv-2604-12045: Thoma, Shen, and He study when sublevel sets of non-convex functions are connected, a property that helps local search avoid isolated valleys and reach global minimisers. Few results establish connectedness outside convexity. Using a toolkit based on the topological mountain pass theorem, they study invex functions, a class including functions satisfying the Polyak-Łojasiewicz inequality and its generalisations. Under mild assumptions, invex sublevel sets are connected. They extend the result to solution sets for invex-incave minimax problems and incave games.
arxiv-2604-12145: Zhang and five colleagues improve audio tokenizers by adding video, a step that usually damages sound reconstruction. They show fusion placement matters most, contrastive learning fails for discrete tokens, and fusing along time rather than feature dimensions works best. Their timing-aware pre-quantization fusion preserves high-fidelity reconstruction while beating audio-only and standard multimodal baselines on understanding tasks.
arxiv-2604-12245: Gómez-Gálvez and three colleagues propose Socrates Loss, a single loss function that unifies classification with confidence calibration by adding an auxiliary unknown class and a dynamic uncertainty penalty. Two-phase methods gain accuracy at the cost of unstable training and poor calibration, while single-loss methods stay stable but underperform. Socrates Loss optimizes both goals at once without scheduled losses, with theory guarding against miscalibration and overfitting, and it often converges faster.
arxiv-2604-12945: Amar Gahir and two colleagues let training data shrink or grow with model feedback. Fixed dropout schedules ignore how learning changes over time. Their method raises or lowers data exposure as training accuracy moves. A light stochastic update tunes the schedule online, balancing exploration and consolidation. Image classification tests cut effective training steps while keeping accuracy competitive with static dropout.
arxiv-2604-13445: Moghe and 13 colleagues study exciton transfer from MoSe2, a two-dimensional semiconductor, to graphene at deep cold. Using picosecond time-resolved light traces on two device types, they find bright exciton lifetimes barely change with graphene layer count. Transfer vanishes when a sub-nanometre hexagonal boron nitride spacer decouples the layers, showing charge tunnelling drives bright exciton relaxation rather than Förster energy transfer. Sub-picosecond Förster transfer still speeds hot exciton relaxation, dimming light beyond lifetime shortening alone.
arxiv-2604-13645: Lei and four colleagues probe why mixing simulation data with scarce real robot data helps generative robot policies, and when it does not. They identify two effects. Structured representation alignment, balancing shared features against domain differences, drives downstream performance. Importance reweighting, which shifts how actions are weighted across domains, plays a smaller role. Toy models and robot manipulation trials confirm both effects, and a simple method built on them beats prior approaches.
arxiv-2604-13945: Alvarado and colleagues treat the hybrid segment of mesoscopic Kitaev chains in full microscopic detail, beyond minimal models. Their treatment captures the quasiparticle range and spin-split Andreev states, changing the coupling picture and yielding renormalized couplings plus sweet-spot conditions. Parity crossings of the bound states mark the best operating windows, where Majorana modes sit well localized with a large gap above them.
arxiv-2604-14045: Sun, Zhang, and He show strong electron correlation can create a zero-field Josephson diode without magnetic order. In a junction with an odd electron count, correlations spontaneously break time-reversal and mirror symmetry, forming a phi-junction with twin energy minima. Spin-orbit coupling breaks spin symmetry but does not set the diode direction, while a tiny Zeeman field tunes the effect, peaking at a level crossing.
arxiv-2604-14445: Jannat, Gowanlock, and Puri run R-tree range queries on commercial memory chips, cutting data-movement cost. Their broadcast method builds the tree bottom-up on the CPU, sends top levels to UPMEM units to filter globally, and farms lower levels out in parallel. On Sports and Lakes data and synthetic tests on up to 2,540 memory units, broadcast execution beats subtree partitioning by keeping communication from swamping work. On Lakes, kernel speedups reach up to 3.66 times over CPU search, while the memory kernel uses roughly a third of the energy.
arxiv-2604-14645: Anusree, Henry, and Nair apply chaos-based feature transforms to convolutional networks starved of training data, where overfitting and thin features hurt accuracy. Logistic, skew tent, and sine maps reshape normalized feature vectors before classification, sharpening class separation without adding trainable parameters. Tested on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10 with varied-depth networks under scarce data, the method beats standalone networks on every dataset. Gains peak at 5.43 percent on MNIST with the skew tent map at 40 samples per class, with about 9 percent on Fashion-MNIST and about 7 percent on CIFAR-10.
arxiv-2604-15045: Dong and colleagues test whether forced sell-offs after mergers really restore competition in United States grocery markets. Stores sold off under such deals lost on average 31 percent of their jobs over five years, through closures and steady shrinkage among survivors. Sales fell too, and the sold stores tended to be weaker assets handed to less capable buyers. The authors argue that leeway over which assets and buyers are picked blunts the remedy.
arxiv-2604-15145: Liu and Zhai build a label-free benchmark for novelty scores of science papers. Existing scores lean on noisy stand-ins like citation counts and review marks, mixing novelty with quality. Their test moves a comparison pool and checks scores under three axioms. Scores must drop as the pool spans more of a paper, climb as it drifts off-topic, and drop as it shifts later. Across ten systems, surface repetition looks solved but conceptual repetition does not, so the authors urge combining embedding and language-model approaches.
arxiv-2604-15245: Pallier, Bonnaire, and Fourcade introduce Goxpyriment, a Go tool for writing behavioral and cognitive experiments. Python tools often burden labs with complex runtime setups that slow rollout. Because Go compiles and embeds assets, Goxpyriment packs each experiment into a single-file binary needing no runtime extras. Its human-friendly design, inspired by Expyriment, ships stimuli from text and shapes to motion clouds.
arxiv-2604-15445: Argüelles and four colleagues prove that decoherence from any scale-invariant setting takes exactly one form: an unparticle bath fixed wholly by the scaling dimension of the coupled operator. All decay and loss exponents follow from that dimension by exact rules that must hold. Tests on unitary Fermi gas transport agree on seven quarters, and a phase change at five halves would shield coherence at long times.
arxiv-2604-15645: Chen and six colleagues offer QPINNACLE, a free multi-GPU tool for physics-aware neural nets, with mixed quantum-classic types. It tests Fourier traits, random weight splits, strict edge rules, tuned loss weights, staged training, and second-order tuning on hyperbolic, flow, and wave tasks. Nets of this kind cost far more than old-style solvers, but mixed quantum types use far fewer weights in some tasks.
arxiv-2604-15745: Cabrera, Andarcia Caballero, and Paulin Fuentes trace the source block in SW-mapped non-commuting U(1) charge theory to a spot inside the Dirac chain. With fixed outside flows in phase space, the Gauss-like second curb births a third-stage hope. That hope matches the pullback of the split of the mapped rule-law lines at first order. For mixed sources, the chain shuts by lever fixing, not by a fourth curb, and trimmed fruits land only in a tight first-class subcase.
arxiv-2604-15845: Lotto, Marchiori, and Conti ask whether timing alone can separate human keystrokes from machine-injected ones, a defense against USB devices like the Rubber Ducky that mimic keyboards to bypass security. Using only hold and flight times, with no key identities or per-user enrollment, they test lightweight classifiers against progressively trickier synthetic attackers. The models discriminate well across generators, and smarter synthesis does not always evade better, supporting content-free, user-agnostic detection.
arxiv-2604-15945: Ridder, Lessel, and Schilling tackle hallucinations in retrieval-augmented generation, where models invent text not backed by retrieved context. Current detectors check outputs after the fact, against frozen inner states. Their RAGognizer approach instead wires a small detection head into the model, so it learns to spot bad output while it learns to write. A companion set, RAGognize, labels hallucinations token by token from real cases. Across benchmarks, the method leads token-level spotting and cuts their rates without harming language quality or relevance.
arxiv-2604-16145: Kang and seven colleagues study training time forecasts for mixed-precision training. Precision strongly affects training time, with swings of more than double over the minimum. Old models rely on static compute graphs that miss mixed precision. Without it, errors reach about 148 percent on the mean absolute percentage error metric. The authors propose a precision-aware model with robust accuracy, with about 10 percent on the same metric.
arxiv-2604-16745: Yang explains why training-free token reduction methods share a cliff-like collapse at compression. A diagnostic framework decomposes the collapse into a signal-agnostic amplifier and pairwise similarity signals. Pairwise ranking consistency falls from zero point eight eight to zero point two seven in deep layers, while unary signals stay stable. Three design principles yield CATIS: unary signals raise the trigger threshold while triage damps the gain. On ViT-Large at 63 percent fewer operations, CATIS keeps about 97 percent of vanilla accuracy, 81 percent, while baselines fall to 43 to 65 percent.
arxiv-2604-16845: Pan and colleagues study diff-aware classification, where the question is whether a correct answer needs spotting group gaps. Safety-tuned models often avoid noting demographic gaps, falling to wrong responses, noes or equal answers. Fine-tuning for accuracy triggers harm drift: explanations grow more harmful as accuracy improves. DART pulls reasoning shaped by labels from a teacher, audits outputs against the baseline, and repairs problematic cases by severity-weighted fine-tuning. On eight benchmarks, accuracy rises from 39 percent to about 69 percent while harm drift cases fall by about 73 percent.
arxiv-2604-17445: Banaian and Huang map the lines along which generalized k-Markov numbers rise steadily. A k-Markov number appears in a positive whole-number solution to a Diophantine equation that gives ordinary Markov numbers when k equals zero. Indexing these numbers by coprime pairs, and extending the labels to non-coprime pairs, the authors chart the rising lines and extend earlier work on the ordinary case. As k grows, a random line is likelier to rise steadily, backing a proposed k-version of Frobenius' uniqueness conjecture.
arxiv-2604-17545: Cline defends the name neutrinoless double beta decay against a recent plea to rename it Majorana double beta decay. The rename proposal aims to credit Majorana and to stress the hoped-for creation of matter in the lab rather than the absence of neutrinos. Cline counters that the current name is more accurate and descriptive, while the case for change lacks credibility. The note weighs naming precision against the suspicion that surrounds past false detection claims.
arxiv-2604-17845: Solanki and six colleagues address beam training for terahertz wireless systems, where ultra-massive antenna arrays use very narrow beams that make alignment costly. Their neural network design learns from received signal powers and codewords from preset hierarchical codebooks, choosing the best transmit and receive beam pair without a constant feedback link. Tests show the approach cuts the complexity of beam design sharply compared with exhaustive and hierarchical search methods.
arxiv-2604-18245: Reitich studies how multi-call language-model protocols both fix and spoil answers. Added calls are usually judged only by net effect, hiding corrections of failures and corruptions of successes. A paired audit records success before and after one operation under a single binary rule, so correction and corruption rates exactly explain the net change. The break-even correction bar climbs steeply with baseline success, and in code tests, adding a helper artifact raised corruptions among 357 passing programs from 28 to 100.
arxiv-2604-18645: Djukanović and five colleagues tackle Variable Gapped Longest Common Subsequence, which loosens classic LCS with flex gaps. The task shows up in gene-string matching with spacing rules, and in time-series work with set delays. They search via root-based state graphs, where the space holds many rooted subgraphs. To tame the blowup, repeated beam search keeps a shared pool of strong root nodes.
